new.cert_about_maine: This certifies that the student passed the Road Ready Maine-format practice test: 30 questions, 24 or more correct. The questions in this format are written to the Maine Driver's License Manual (Rev. 4/24) and Title 29-A (Motor Vehicles).

Maine law says 2 years or until you turn 21, whichever comes later. The 2 years start on the day the license is issued.

guide_lic_q1.old: You get your first license at 16. How long is it a provisional license?

guide_lic_q1_why.old: The 270 days are the intermediate rules. The provisional period is 2 years from the day the license is issued.
guide_lic_q1_why.new: The 270 days are the intermediate rules. The suspension rule for moving violations lasts 2 years from the day the license is issued. The law keeps the name "provisional" until you turn 21.

debrief_speeding_one.new: ⚠️ Speed limit exceeded for {s}s total ({n} separate incident). Remember: double the speed needs about 4 times the braking distance. A little faster means a lot more room to stop.

moosesafety_exp5.old: Pull over safely and collect yourself. Adrenaline tunnel-vision is real and lasts 3–5 minutes. Driving on immediately means your scanning and reaction time are worse, not better. If you hit the moose — even a glancing strike — call the Maine Warden Service (911) and stay put; injured moose in the road kill more people than the first hit.
moosesafety_exp5.new: Pull over safely and collect yourself. After a scare your body is tense, and you scan and react worse for a few minutes. If you hit the moose, even lightly, call 911 and stay clear of it. An injured moose is dangerous, and another driver can hit it.

railroadcrossing_exp2.old: Never try to beat a train. Large objects look slower than they actually are — a train looking "a ways off" is usually doing 50+ mph and moving 80+ ft/sec. If your engine stalls mid-crossing (a real risk at low-speed crossings), the train cannot stop for you: at 55 mph it needs more than a mile.
railroadcrossing_exp2.new: Never try to beat a train. A large object looks slower than it is, so a train that looks far away can reach you very soon. If your engine stalls on the crossing, the train cannot stop for you: at 55 mph it needs more than a mile.

all_season_tires_lose_roughly_40_of_th.old: All-season rubber starts stiffening below about 45°F (7°C) — that is the industry threshold where a winter tire begins to out-grip it, and it is well above freezing, so the window opens earlier in the fall than most people expect. Winter compounds stay pliable: on packed snow at 30 mph a winter tire stops in roughly 59 ft where an all-season needs about 30 ft more — two car lengths. Maine law allows studs Oct 1–May 1.
all_season_tires_lose_roughly_40_of_th.new: All-season rubber gets stiff in the cold and loses grip. Winter tires use softer rubber that stays flexible, so they grip better on snow, ice and cold pavement. A common rule of thumb is to switch when days stay below about 45°F (7°C). That is well above freezing. Maine law allows studded tires from October 2 to April 30 (29-A §1919).

congratulations_you_have_a_full_maine_.old: Congratulations. The intermediate restrictions have ended. Your license is still provisional: for 2 years after you got it, a moving-violation conviction suspends it for 30 days (longer for a repeat). Drive responsibly — Maine roads count on you.
congratulations_you_have_a_full_maine_.new: Congratulations. The intermediate restrictions have ended. Your license is still provisional. For 2 years after you got it, a conviction for a moving violation suspends it for 30 days (longer if it happens again). Until you turn 21, you may not drive with any alcohol in your body. Drive with care. Maine roads count on you.

gdl_stage_provisional_desc.old: The 270-day rules have ended. Your license is still provisional through {date}. Until then, a conviction for a moving violation suspends it: 30 days the first time, 180 days the second time, and 1 year after that.
gdl_stage_provisional_desc.new: The 270-day rules have ended. Your license is still provisional. The 2-year rule lasts through {date}. Until then, a conviction for a moving violation suspends your license: 30 days the first time, 180 days the second time, and 1 year after that. If you turn 21 after that date, the law keeps the name "provisional" until your 21st birthday.

gdl_stage_after_desc.old: The 2-year provisional suspension rule covered your first 2 years. That time has passed. Demerit points and every traffic law still apply. If you are under 21, you still may not drive with any alcohol in your body.
gdl_stage_after_desc.new: The 2-year suspension rule for new drivers covered your first 2 years. That time has passed. Demerit points and every traffic law still apply. If you are under 21, the law still calls your license provisional, and you still may not drive with any alcohol in your body.

gdl_dates_prov_until.old: Your license is provisional through {date}. Days left: {n}.
gdl_dates_prov_until.new: The 2-year rule for new drivers lasts through {date}. Days left: {n}.

gdl_dates_prov_ended.new: The 2-year rule for new drivers ended on {date}.

gdl_dates_note.old: These dates count from the license date you entered. If you are convicted of breaking a 270-day rule, those rules last 270 more days.
gdl_dates_note.new: These dates count from the license date you entered. If you are convicted of breaking a 270-day rule, those rules last 270 more days. Maine law also calls a first license provisional until age 21, when that comes later than the 2-year date.

gdl_dates_empty.old: Enter the date of your first license above. You will see when the 270-day rules and the 2-year provisional period end.
gdl_dates_empty.new: Enter the date of your first license above. You will see when the 270-day rules and the 2-year rule for new drivers end.

postcrash_get_medically_checked_even_if_.old: Get medically checked even if you feel fine. Concussion, whiplash, soft tissue damage: 24-48 hour delay is normal.
postcrash_get_medically_checked_even_if_.new: See a doctor or nurse if you feel any pain, even later. Some injuries do not hurt right away.

postcrash_call_your_insurance_within_24_.old: Call YOUR insurance within 24 hours. Give them the police report number if one was issued. Do NOT give recorded statements to the OTHER driver's insurance without your agent present.
postcrash_call_your_insurance_within_24_.new: Tell your insurance company about the crash soon. Give them the police report number if one was issued.

postcrash_do_not_post_about_it_on_social.old: Do NOT post about it on social media. Insurance adjusters screenshot these. "Cool, I'm totally fine!" can void your injury claim.
postcrash_do_not_post_about_it_on_social.new: Do NOT post about it on social media. Write down what happened while you remember it: the time, the place, the weather and the road.

postcrash_keep_every_receipt_tow_rental_.old: Keep every receipt: tow, rental, medical co-pays, lost work. All reimbursable.
postcrash_keep_every_receipt_tow_rental_.new: Keep your papers from the crash: the tow bill, repair bills and medical bills.

postcrash_journal_your_pain_and_limitati.old: Journal your pain and limitations daily. Memory fades; notes don't.
postcrash_journal_your_pain_and_limitati.new: Talk with a parent or guardian about what happened and how you feel. A crash is upsetting.

before_opening_your_door_in_traffic_us.old: Before opening your door in traffic, use your FAR hand — your right hand from the driver seat in the U.S. — so your body naturally turns to check behind. Dooring is one of the most common urban bike crashes — studies put it at 12-27% of city car-bike collisions (Chicago logged 19.7% of cycling injuries in 2011).
before_opening_your_door_in_traffic_us.new: Before opening your door in traffic, use your FAR hand — your right hand from the driver seat in the U.S. — so your body naturally turns to check behind. A door opened into a cyclist's path is a common city bike crash.

3_142_distracted_driving_deaths_in_the.old: . At 55 mph, NHTSA compares that to driving a football-field length blind. Talking on a handheld phone roughly quadruples your crash risk — but TEXTING is in a different category again: the Virginia Tech naturalistic driving studies put it near 23×, because it takes your eyes, hands, and attention at the same time. NHTSA also reports 3,208 distracted-driving deaths and 315,167 injuries in 2024.
3_142_distracted_driving_deaths_in_the.new: . At 55 mph, NHTSA compares that to driving a football-field length blind. Talking on a handheld phone roughly quadruples your crash risk — but TEXTING is in a different category again: a Virginia Tech study of truck drivers put it near 23×, because it takes your eyes, hands, and attention at the same time. NHTSA also reports 3,208 distracted-driving deaths and 315,167 injuries in 2024.

roundabouts_reduce_fatal_crashes_by_90.old: Roundabouts reduce fatal crashes by 90% vs. signaled intersections. Here is how to use them.
roundabouts_reduce_fatal_crashes_by_90.new: Roundabouts are safer than signals: U.S. studies found 72% to 80% fewer injury crashes (IIHS). Here is how to use them.

roundabouts_reduce_fatal_crashes_by_90_2.old: Roundabouts reduce fatal crashes by 90% vs. signals. Once you get used to them, they are faster and safer.
roundabouts_reduce_fatal_crashes_by_90_2.new: U.S. studies found 72% to 80% fewer injury crashes after intersections were changed to roundabouts (IIHS). Once you get used to them, they are faster and safer.

left_turns_are_the_1_most_dangerous_co.old: Left turns are the #1 most dangerous common maneuver. NHTSA puts about 53% of CROSSING-PATH crashes — the head-on-into-turning kind — at or just after a left turn, against roughly 1% for right turns. You are crossing oncoming traffic instead of merging with it.
left_turns_are_the_1_most_dangerous_co.new: A left turn is one of the riskiest common moves. You cross oncoming traffic instead of merging with it. Wait for a gap you are sure of.

smooth_driving_no_jackrabbits_coast_to.old: • Smooth driving (no jackrabbits, coast to stops) improves real-world MPG by 20-40% over the EPA sticker.
smooth_driving_no_jackrabbits_coast_to.new: • Smooth driving saves fuel. Fast starts and hard braking can lower gas mileage by 10% to 40% in stop-and-go traffic (fueleconomy.gov).

alcohol_shrinks_your_visual_field_by_u.old: • Alcohol shrinks your visual field by up to 25% at night — tunnel vision + slow reaction = deadly.
alcohol_shrinks_your_visual_field_by_u.new: • Alcohol makes it harder to see at night and slows your reactions. Together that is deadly.

permit_q29_exp.old: Rapid acceleration and hard braking can lower MPG by 15-40%. Every time you brake hard, you turn kinetic energy into heat — wasted fuel.
permit_q29_exp.new: Fast starts and hard braking waste gas. They can lower your gas mileage by roughly 15% to 30% at highway speeds and 10% to 40% in stop-and-go traffic (fueleconomy.gov). Each time you brake hard, the energy of the moving car turns into heat. That fuel is wasted.

permit_q31_exp.old: Below ~40 mph rolling resistance dominates. Above it, aerodynamic drag takes over. Peak MPG for a gasoline car usually falls in a broad 30-55 mph plateau, often near 40 mph. Crawling is not better: an idling engine burns fuel per SECOND, so very low speeds cost more per mile.
permit_q31_exp.new: Below about 40 mph, most of the fuel goes to rolling the tires. Above it, pushing through the air costs the most. A gasoline car usually gets its best MPG somewhere between 30 and 55 mph, often near 40 mph. Crawling is not better: an idling engine burns fuel every SECOND, so very low speeds cost more per mile.

permit_q176_exp.new: The person who supervises a Maine permit holder must be a licensed driver who is at least 20 and has held a license for at least 2 years. Parents often do this, but another family member or adult who meets the rule can too. The supervisor sits in the front passenger seat.

permit_q178_q.old: A round yellow sign with a black "X" and the letters "RR" warns of:
permit_q178_q.new: What does a round yellow sign with a black "X" and the letters "RR" warn of?

permit_q179_exp.old: Blue = motorist services. Includes gas, food, lodging, hospital, rest area, EV charging. Different from green (directions) and brown (recreational/scenic).
permit_q179_exp.new: Blue signs show services for drivers: gas, food, lodging, hospitals, rest areas and EV charging. Green signs give directions. Brown signs show parks and scenic places.

permit_q181_exp.old: Maine law (Title 12, §13106-A(6) and (7)): a snowmobile must come to a COMPLETE STOP before entering a public way, and must yield right-of-way to ALL vehicular traffic. Cross as directly as possible, on a marked or designated crossing where one exists. As a driver: a stopped sled at a trail crossing has to yield to you, but treat it as a vehicle that may pull out anyway — sleds are quiet, low, and easy to lose against a snowbank.
permit_q181_exp.new: Maine law (Title 12, §13106-A(6) and (7)): a snowmobile must come to a COMPLETE STOP before it enters a public way. It must yield to ALL vehicle traffic. It must cross as directly as possible, at a marked crossing where there is one. As a driver, know that a stopped sled at a trail crossing has to yield to you. Still, treat it as a vehicle that may pull out anyway. Sleds are quiet and low, and they are hard to see against a snowbank.

permit_q182_q.old: You are driving on a rural Maine road at night and approach a marked snowmobile crossing. You should:

permit_q184_exp.old: Maine requires an ANNUAL safety inspection at a Maine BMV/State-Police-licensed inspection station. The sticker goes on the inside of the windshield, lower-left, and shows the month and year it expires. Driving with an expired sticker is a citation.
permit_q184_exp.new: Maine requires an ANNUAL safety inspection (once a year) at a licensed inspection station. The sticker goes on the inside of the windshield, at the lower left. It shows the month and year it expires. You can get a ticket for driving with an expired sticker.

permit_q185_exp.old: Maine law caps the standard inspection fee at $12.50 (29-A §1751). Cars registered in Cumberland County need an enhanced inspection that can cost more: up to $18.50 for 1996 and newer models. Pay it at any licensed inspection station — independent garages and dealerships hold most of the licenses.
permit_q185_exp.new: Maine law caps the standard inspection fee at $12.50 (29-A §1751). Cars registered in Cumberland County need an enhanced inspection. It can cost more: up to $18.50 for 1996 and newer models. You pay at any licensed inspection station. Most are garages and car dealers.

permit_q188_q.old: You hit a deer on a rural Maine road and the animal is killed. Maine law requires you to:
permit_q188_q.new: You hit a deer on a rural Maine road and the animal is killed. What does Maine law require you to do?

permit_q188_exp.old: Maine Title 12 §12403: report a collision with a deer, moose, bear or wild turkey to a law enforcement officer BY THE QUICKEST MEANS. If the officer finds your vehicle has apparent damage, they issue a certificate giving you ownership of the carcass — and you must then take the WHOLE animal, not the parts you want. Failing to report, or removing part of a carcass without that certificate, is a civil violation carrying a $100–$500 fine. To report it, call 911.
permit_q188_exp.new: Maine Title 12 §12403: report a collision with a deer, moose, bear or wild turkey to a law enforcement officer BY THE QUICKEST MEANS. To report it, call 911. If the officer finds that your vehicle has apparent damage, the officer gives you a certificate. The certificate makes the carcass yours. You must then take the WHOLE animal, not only the parts you want. Failing to report, or removing part of a carcass without that certificate, is a civil violation carrying a $100–$500 fine.

permit_q191_q.new: After a winter of road salt, which area of your car is most likely to rust?

permit_q192_q.new: You hit a deep pothole at speed in early Maine spring and feel the steering pull to one side. What is the most likely problem?

permit_q195_exp.old: A steady red arrow means traffic making the turn the arrow shows must stop and wait until the arrow changes to green.
permit_q195_exp.new: A steady red arrow means stop if you want to turn the way the arrow points. Wait until the arrow turns green.

permit_q207_exp.old: With one solid and one dashed yellow line, passing is allowed only for traffic that has the dashed line on its side, and only when it is safe.
permit_q207_exp.new: Sometimes one yellow line is solid and the other is dashed. Then only traffic with the dashed line on its side may pass, and only when it is safe.

permit_q213_exp.old: You may not pass where a yellow pennant NO PASSING ZONE sign is on the left of the road, or where a white rectangular DO NOT PASS sign is on the right.
permit_q213_exp.new: A yellow pennant sign on the left of the road says NO PASSING ZONE. A white rectangular sign on the right says DO NOT PASS. You may not pass where you see either sign.

permit_q218_exp.old: A visual distraction makes you look away from the road at something that has nothing to do with driving, such as a billboard or a crash scene.
permit_q218_exp.new: A visual distraction makes you look away from the road. You look at something that has nothing to do with driving, such as a billboard or a crash scene.

permit_q219_exp.old: A manual distraction takes one or both hands off the wheel for something that is not driving: eating, drinking, tuning the radio, or setting a GPS.
permit_q219_exp.new: A manual distraction takes one or both hands off the wheel. Your hands do something that is not driving. Examples are eating, drinking, tuning the radio and setting a GPS.

permit_q220_exp.old: Cognitive distractions are thoughts and feelings, such as anger, anxiety, or worry, that pull your attention away from the road.
permit_q220_exp.new: Cognitive distractions are thoughts and feelings that pull your mind away from the road. Anger, anxiety and worry are examples.

permit_q227_exp.old: The manual says using a phone or other device in a moving vehicle can lead to crashes as critical and as devastating as those caused by impaired driving.
permit_q227_exp.new: The manual says that using a phone or other device in a moving vehicle can cause crashes. Those crashes can be as serious as the ones that impaired drivers cause.

permit_q239_exp.old: Headlights show about 250 feet. The manual's chart gives a total stopping distance of 188 feet at 50 mph and 272 feet at 60 mph, so above about 50 mph you cannot stop inside the distance you can see.
permit_q239_exp.new: Headlights show about 250 feet. The manual's chart gives a total stopping distance of 188 feet at 50 mph and 272 feet at 60 mph. So above about 50 mph you cannot stop inside the distance you can see.

permit_q242_exp.old: A conviction for a moving violation while your license is provisional brings a 30-day suspension the first time. Second and third offenses bring longer suspensions.
permit_q242_exp.new: If you are convicted of a moving violation while your license is provisional, you get a 30-day suspension the first time. The second and third times, the suspension is longer.

permit_q243_exp.old: Provisional license suspensions for moving violations: 30 days for the first, 180 days for the second, and one year for the third or later.
permit_q243_exp.new: A moving violation suspends a provisional license. The first time it is for 30 days. The second time it is for 180 days. The third time or later it is for one year.

permit_q251_exp.old: Maine law requires every owner and operator of a motor vehicle to have liability insurance and to show evidence of it when a law enforcement officer asks. Carry the insurance card in the vehicle.
permit_q251_exp.new: Maine law says every owner and every driver of a motor vehicle must have liability insurance. You must show proof of it when a police officer asks. Keep the insurance card in the vehicle.

kinetic_content.old: A moving car stores energy — kinetic energy. KE = ½mv². Notice the v-squared again. At 30 mph a car has some kinetic energy. At 60 mph it has FOUR TIMES that. At 90 mph it has NINE TIMES. Every bit of that has to go somewhere in a crash — into crumple zones, airbags, and unfortunately, into people. This is the single biggest reason speed limits exist. Modern crumple zones are designed for ~35 mph impacts. Above that, the occupants start to see forces that human bodies cannot survive. Seatbelts, airbags, and crumple zones together cut fatality risk by ~75% at legal speeds — but they cannot fight physics forever.

hypermiling_content.old: Hypermiling is the art of squeezing every mile from a gallon. Proven techniques: (1) Gentle accel — imagine an egg between your foot and the pedal. (2) Anticipate — read the road 20-30 seconds ahead so you brake less. (3) Coast to stops — fuel cut-off activates when you lift off the gas, meaning coasting in gear uses ZERO fuel on modern cars. (4) Pulse and glide — gently accelerate, then coast. Works best under 45 mph. (5) Highway cruise at 55-60 mph, not 75 (drag is brutal). (6) Tires at door-sticker PSI. (7) Remove the roof box when not using it. (8) Don't idle — modern engines restart on <0.5 s of fuel, so 30+ sec of idling wastes more than restarting. Combined, these techniques can boost real-world MPG by 20-40% over aggressive driving. Free money.

(4) Pulse and glide — gently accelerate, then coast. Works best under 45 mph. (5) Highway cruise at 55-60 mph, not 75 (drag is brutal). (6) Tires at door-sticker PSI. (7) Remove the roof box when not using it. (8) Don't idle — modern engines restart on <0.5 s of fuel, so 30+ sec of idling wastes more than restarting. Aggressive driving can lower gas mileage by roughly 15% to 30% at highway speeds and 10% to 40% in stop-and-go traffic (fueleconomy.gov). Driving smoothly gets that back. Free money.
